description: cert_basic_constraints() and has_key_cert_sign() both return None on DER decode errors. The callers treat None as 'constraint not met' — None from cert_basic_constraints triggers NotCA, None from has_key_cert_sign triggers KeyUsageMissing. This fail-closed pattern is correct for a security-critical library: a cert with an undecodable BasicConstraints extension will be rejected rather than silently accepted. A contributor might argue 'we should return Err on decode failure for better diagnostics' — but that would complicate the calling code, potentially add new error paths, and create the question of what index to attach to the error. The current design sacrifices a small amount of diagnostic precision for simplicity and correctness. Worth defending.
title: fail-closed design throughout: decode errors treated as absent
